---
title: Token Factory Sandboxes
description: Public repositories and dry runs are verified on Nebius Token Factory Sandboxes, microVMs Teire builds its own images in. Private repositories stay on Cloudflare Containers.
icon: Box
---

Teire verifies a public repository's upgrade, and every dry run, on **Nebius Token Factory Sandboxes**: each command runs in its own microVM, a virtual machine with its own kernel. The same install, typecheck and tests run as on [Cloudflare Containers](/docs/build/security), with the same evidence rules ([Verification](/docs/build/verification)).

## Which runs go where

| Repository | Backend | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Public | Token Factory Sandboxes | A saved sandbox image keeps the repository's files for 180 days, and Token Factory has no call to delete it. For public code that is no exposure. |
| Dry run of a public repository | Token Factory Sandboxes | The same reason |
| Private | Cloudflare Containers | A private repository's files never land in an image that outlives the run |

When Token Factory isn't available to the worker (no project, or `whoami` grants no spawn), a public run verifies on Cloudflare Containers instead. The run page and its receipt name the backend each run used.

## How a run works there

Token Factory Sandboxes runs one command per microVM. A microVM that is kept saves what it changed as a new image, and the next command starts from that image. Teire chains them:

<Steps>
<Step>
**The image.** Teire builds its sandbox images inside Token Factory, from the same Dockerfiles as the Cloudflare images: it imports the public base image, runs the build steps in one microVM, and tags the result by the recipe's hash, so each image is built once.
</Step>
<Step>
**The checkout.** The worker streams the commit's tarball into Token Factory's upload as it arrives (no repository code runs on the worker, and the tarball is never held in its memory; it stops past 200 MB), then unpacks it into `/work` in a kept microVM.
</Step>
<Step>
**The install, with the network on.** Your package manager installs from its registries. The result is the image the checks start from.
</Step>
<Step>
**The checks, with the network off.** Each check runs in a microVM with **no network interface at all**, as the unprivileged user `teire` (uid 10001), as CI runs them. The first check starts from the install's image and each later check from the image the one before it left, so a build's output (generated files, compiled code) reaches the tests, as it does in a single container. Each command runs under GNU `timeout`, so a check that hangs ends with exit 124 inside the microVM. The agent's edits between attempts are uploaded and placed into each check's microVM.
</Step>
</Steps>

Measured on `teire-dev/examples` (2026-10-28), each baseline on its own image built inside Token Factory:

| Folder | Ecosystem | Install | Checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `npm-zod` | npm | 4.9 s | typecheck, 4/4 tests |
| `py-major` | Python (uv) | 4.9 s | 2/2 tests |
| `go-major` | Go | 2.6 s | build, `go vet`, 4/4 tests |
| `rust-major` | Cargo | 4.9 s | build, 5/5 tests |
| `ruby-major` | Bundler | 4.9 s | 6/6 tests |
| `jvm-major` | Maven, JDK 17 | 51.9 s | compile, 4/4 tests |

Limits come from Token Factory's own `whoami` call, never assumed: an hour per microVM, 50 at a time and 8 image imports at a time, which Teire keeps to (spawns and imports wait for a free slot, shared by every run on the worker); `whoami` also reports 12 GB per image layer. Measured from inside a microVM: 4 CPUs, 3.9 GB of memory, a 2 GB `/dev/shm`. A failed spawn is not retried, because spawns carry no idempotency key. Teire follows each command through the operation's server-sent events (a quiet stream is checked against the operation's state); a run that is closed cancels the operations it still has running.

## What differs from Cloudflare Containers

| | Token Factory Sandboxes | Cloudflare Containers |
|---|---|---|
| Isolation | A microVM per command | A container per side, driven by a Durable Object |
| Install network | Open (no allowlist exists) | Package registries only, GET only |
| Check network | None: no network interface | Off; any request is denied and recorded |
| Egress record | None kept by Token Factory | Every request the sandbox refused |
| After the run | Images kept 180 days, no delete call | The container is destroyed |

<Callout title="Gaps that shape how Teire uses it">
Token Factory Sandboxes has no call to delete an image, no idempotency key on spawns, no egress log and no allowlist for the install's network. Each shapes how Teire uses it: public repositories only, spawns never retried, and checks with no network interface.

One more, found on a real fork (`teire-dev/bristow`): the microVM's root filesystem (virtiofs) loses a file a Ruby native-extension build writes while the compiler it started holds it open, so every native gem failed with `Errno::EBADF` on `mkmf.log`. The same build passes on the microVM's tmpfs, so on Token Factory Teire builds gems there and copies them into place.
</Callout>
